sampled_files..github/workflows/ci.yml:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, "feature/*"]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  # Merge queue: queue builds check out gh-readonly-queue/... refs and run
  # the SAME required checks on the speculative merge. Without this trigger
  # the queue waits for checks that are never reported — the silent stall.
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]

jobs:
  leak-gate:
    name: Leak gate (gitleaks + forbidden files)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4
      - name: No secret-bearing files in the tree
        run: |
          FOUND=$(find . \( -name ".env" -o -name ".env.local" -o -name ".env.production" -o -name "*.pem" -o -name "id_rsa*" -o -name "*.p12" \) -not -path "./.git/*")
          if [ -n "$FOUND" ]; then echo "Forbidden files:"; echo "$FOUND"; exit 1; fi
      - name: gitleaks (CLI direkt — die Action verlangt fuer Orgs einen Lizenz-Key)
        run: |
          docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/repo" \
            ghcr.io/gitleaks/gitleaks@sha256:b109bc5f8f76a38196a3e413704fc5b9e3c32360bce4e4b603bd6f45b3721dbb \
            dir /repo --no-banner --exit-code 1
      # Namen statt Adressen: die eigene Flotte des Autors. gitleaks oben faehrt
      # Null-Toleranz fuer /Users/<name>, 100.64.0.0/10 und *.ts.net — der Baum
      # ist darunter sauber. Bei den Agentennamen ist er das NICHT, darum hier
      # eine Baseline (docs/privacy-sweep-backlog.md): heute gruen, aber jede
      # NEUE Fundstelle rot.
      - name: privacy-scan (Flottennamen gegen die Baseline)
        run: python3 scripts/privacy-scan.py

  backend:
    name: Backend Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: backend
    steps:
      # fetch-depth: 0 (full history, all branches) — not the v4 default of a
      # shallow single-ref clone. test_alembic_chain_integrity.py diffs HEAD
      # against `origin/main` to find migrations new on this branch; with the
      # default shallow checkout, `origin/main` isn't fetched at all, the diff
      # can't run, and the destructive-migration guards below silently SKIP
      # instead of running — exactly the CI job where they're supposed to have
      # teeth (task 40c484c6, a depth-1 repro on task 3f249d2b: 205
      # passed / 1 skipped / job green).
      - uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      # Same pinned versions as the backend image (backend/Dockerfile):
      # the lock first, then the app itself without re-resolving anything.
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          pip install -r requirements.lock
          pip install --no-deps -e .

      - name: Run tests
        run: pytest -x --tb=short -q -n auto

  backend-postgres:
    name: Backend Tests (Postgres lane)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: backend
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: test
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: test
          POSTGRES_DB: test
        ports: ["5432:5432"]
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U test"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10
    env:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql+asyncpg://test:test@localhost:5432/test
      MC_TEST_DATABASE_URL: postgresql+asyncpg://test:test@localhost:5432/test
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4

      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      # Same pinned versions as the backend image (backend/Dockerfile):
      # the lock first, then the app itself without re-resolving anything.
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          pip install -r requirements.lock
          pip install --no-deps -e .

      # The real schema — migrations, plpgsql trigger validate_task_transition,
      # indexes. The SQLite lane never runs any of this (W0.2, 10.09.2026).
      - name: Apply migrations
        run: alembic upgrade head

      - name: Run Postgres-only tests
        run: pytest -x --tb=short -q -m postgres

  omp-bridge:
    name: omp-bridge Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4

      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      # tests/test_acp_through_tests.py imports app.services.omp_chat — the
      # bridge's own suite reaches into the backend package for that one
      # shared parser, so backend's deps must be importable too (PR #547
      # follow-up W3: this lane didn't exist before, so the 6 new
      # test_acp_workspace_parity.py tests + the sabotage probes in
      # test_acp_through_tests.py never ran in CI at all).
      - name: Install backend dependencies (tests import app.services.omp_chat)
        working-directory: backend
        run: pip install -r requirements.lock && pip install --no-deps -e .

      - name: Run omp-bridge tests
        working-directory: docker/omp-bridge
        env:
          # entrypoint.sh renders this at container boot; the test suite
          # needs it too (_acp_model_selector fails loud without it, ADR-054).
          OPENAI_MODEL: ci-test-model
        run: python3 -m pytest tests/ -q

  cdp-gateway:
    name: cdp-gateway Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4

      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      # Same version pinned in docker/cdp-browser/Dockerfile, plus the test
      # deps (httpx for the integration suite's own client, pytest-asyncio
      # for both suites). No backend/frontend deps needed — this module is
      # deliberately stdlib + websockets only (bauplan.md B1).
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pip install "websockets==15.0.1" httpx pytest pytest-asyncio

      - name: Run cdp-gateway tests
        working-directory: docker/cdp-browser/gateway
        run: python3 -m pytest . -q

  mc-cli:
    name: mc-cli Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4

      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      # The suite is stdlib-only besides pytest (task 234, 2026-09-17:
      # 234 test functions / 245 collected items, 245 passed in <1s under
      # CI-like conditions — fresh clone, empty HOME, no MC_* env, no
      # backend, no ~/.mc). tests/conftest.py redirects MC_CONTEXT_ENV_PATH
      # per test, so the lane never touches a host-shared context file, and
      # every HTTP client is mocked or a local stub server — no services
      # needed. Blocking from day one: the suite measured 100% green before
      # the lane was switched on.
      - name: Install pytest
        run: pip install pytest

      - name: Run mc-cli tests
        run: python3 -m pytest scripts/mc-cli/tests -q --tb=short

  frontend-v2:
    name: Frontend Checks
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: frontend-v2
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"  # muss zum Runtime-Image passen (frontend Dockerfile: node:22)
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend-v2/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: TypeScript check
        run: npx tsc --noEmit

      - name: Run tests
        run: npm run test:run

  deploy-portability:
    name: Fresh-boot E2E (setup.sh → migrations → register)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4
      # No "chmod 777 ~/.mc" here any more: the runner user is uid 1001, the
      # image default is 1000 — exactly the fresh-Linux case that used to crash
      # migration 0112. setup.sh now writes PUID/PGID from `id -u`/`id -g` and
      # the backend runs as the runner's uid; this job proves it end to end.
      - name: docker compose config validates
        run: |
          ./setup.sh   # nur fuer die config-Validierung; install.sh ruft es erneut (idempotent)
          docker compose config -q
      - name: setup.ps1 parses under Windows PowerShell rules
        shell: pwsh
        # ParseFile statt scriptblock::Create — findet auch die Fehlerklasse
        # "UTF-8 ohne BOM + Nicht-ASCII wird unter PS 5.1 zu Smart-Quotes"
        # (live auf einem echten Windows gefunden, 2026-08-05). Das Script
        # ist deshalb bewusst ASCII-only.
        run: |
          $bytes = [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("setup.ps1")
          $nonAscii = $bytes | Where-Object { $_ -gt 127 }
          if ($nonAscii) { throw "setup.ps1 must stay ASCII-only (PS 5.1 reads BOM-less UTF-8 as ANSI): $($nonAscii.Count) bytes > 127" }
          $errs = $null
          $null = [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile("$PWD/setup.ps1", [ref]$null, [ref]$errs)
          if ($errs.Count -gt 0) { $errs | ForEach-Object { Write-Error $_.Message }; exit 1 }
      - name: Remote-access step (install.sh / setup.sh) — tests + shellcheck
        # scripts/lib/remote-access.sh decides whether MC listens on the
        # network; an unattended install must never open it (ci-safe test).
        run: |
          bash scripts/tests/test_remote_access.sh
          shellcheck -x -S warning install.sh setup.sh scripts/lib/remote-access.sh scripts/open-network.sh scripts/tests/test_remote_access.sh
      - name: install.sh — the advertised one-liner IS the tested path
        # Baut + bootet den vollen Stack, laeuft Migrationen, wartet auf health.
        #
        # BUILD_MIN_FREE_GB hier (nicht auf Job-Ebene) gesetzt: GitHub-hosted
        # Runner haben per Doku ~14 GB frei, die lokale 15-GB-Schwelle wuerde
        # diesen Bau also garantiert und FALSCH verweigern. 5 GB ist die
        # ehrliche Zahl fuer das, was dieser Stack wirklich braucht. Auf
        # Job-Ebene gesetzt wuerde die Variable ausserdem in den
        # Lib-Test-Step unten lecken und dort Test 7 (.env-Schwelle) verdecken.
        env:
          BUILD_MIN_FREE_GB: "5"
        run: ./install.sh --here
      - name: install.sh — shellcheck + release-pinning helpers
        # The one-liner a user runs unseen via curl | bash. shellcheck -x
        # follows the sourced disk-preflight library. The helper tests run
        # against a local git repo and file:// "API" answers, so they are
        # deterministic and need no GitHub API quota.
        run: |
          shellcheck -x -S warning install.sh scripts/release-image-tags.sh   # info-level notes differ between shellcheck versions
          pip install -q pytest
          python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --noconftest backend/tests/test_install_release_pinning.py backend/tests/test_release_image_tags.py
      - name: --here ran the checkout, not a published image
        # CI has no release that matches the branch under test, so --here
        # must take the edge path: MC_IMAGE_TAG=edge (a tag no registry
        # publishes) and a local build. If it ever pulled a release image
        # instead, this job would test old code and stay green.
        run: |
          grep -qx 'MC_CHANNEL=edge' .env
          grep -qx 'MC_IMAGE_TAG=edge' .env
          img="$(docker inspect --format '{{.Config.Image}}' "$(docker compose ps -q backend)")"
          echo "backend runs: $img"
          test "$img" = "ghcr.io/argyelan-ai/mc-backend:edge"
          docker compose exec -T -u mcuser backend test -f /app/app/worker.py
      - name: Register first admin + authenticated API call
        run: |
          TOKEN=$(curl -sf -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/auth/register \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d '{"email":"ci@example.com","password":"ci-test-password-123","name":"CI"}' \
            | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['access_token'])")
          test -n "$TOKEN"
          curl -sf -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8000/api/v1/boards >/dev/null
          echo "fresh-boot E2E OK"
      - name: Fresh install seeds no example hardware and no demo agent
        # Migrations + boot seeders on an empty database: only the cloud
        # provider anchors from runtimes.json, no runtime on a host address,
        # no host, no agent (test_fresh_install_seed.py is the unit side).
        run: |
          q() { docker compose exec -T db psql -U mc -d mission_control -Atc "$1"; }
          echo "runtimes: $(q "select string_agg(slug, ',' order by slug) from runtimes")"
          test "$(q "select count(*) from agents")" = "0"
          test "$(q "select count(*) from hosts")" = "0"
          test "$(q "select count(*) from runtimes where endpoint !~ '^https://'")" = "0"
          test "$(q "select count(*) from runtimes")" = "$(python3 -c 'import json; print(len(json.load(open("backend/config/runtimes.json"))))')"
          echo "fresh-install seed OK"
      - name: Host uid != 1000 — backend writes ~/.mc as the runner user
        run: |
          echo "runner uid=$(id -u) gid=$(id -g)"
          grep -E '^P(U|G)ID=' .env
          HEALTH=$(curl -sf http://localhost:8000/health)
          echo "$HEALTH"
          echo "$HEALTH" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); assert d["status"] == "ok", d'
          # Created by the backend's boot step (not by setup.sh) → must belong to us.
          test "$(stat -c %u ~/.mc/vault)" = "$(id -u)"
          test "$(stat -c %u ~/.mc/wake-requests)" = "$(id -u)"
          echo "host-uid E2E OK"
      - name: Host uid matrix (entrypoint remap, readable failure, PUID=0 refused)
        run: bash scripts/test-host-uid.sh
      - name: Logs on failure
        if: failure()
        run: docker compose logs backend db --tail=80

  docker:
    name: Docker Build Check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4

      # Jeder `docker build` hier ist ein Bau-Weg und bekommt denselben
      # Preflight wie jeder lokale Weg. BUILD_MIN_FREE_GB=5 statt der lokalen
      # 15: GitHub-hosted Runner haben per Doku ~14 GB frei, die lokale
      # Schwelle wuerde hier garantiert und FALSCH verweigern. Bewusst pro
      # Step statt auf Job-Ebene — job-weit gesetzt leckt die Variable in die
      # Lib-Test-Steps unten und verdeckt dort Test 7 (.env-Schwelle).
      - name: Build backend image
        env:
          BUILD_MIN_FREE_GB: "5"
        run: |
          . ./docker/shared/disk-preflight.sh
          mc_disk_preflight
          docker build -t mc-backend-test ./backend

      # Plattenplatz-Preflight (docker/shared/disk-preflight.sh). Two lanes,
      # because the library is sourced by bash entry points AND by scripts
      # running under BusyBox ash — a bashism that only shows up on alpine is
      # exactly the class the context-detect lane below exists for. The host
      # lane runs under /bin/sh (dash on ubuntu-latest), which catches the
      # POSIX violations; the alpine lane pins the actual musl runtime.
      - name: Disk preflight lib tests (host /bin/sh)
        run: sh docker/shared/test_disk_preflight.sh

      - name: Disk preflight lib tests (BusyBox/musl)
        run: |
          docker run --rm \
            -v "$PWD/docker/shared/disk-preflight.sh:/lib.sh:ro" \
            -v "$PWD/docker/shared/test_disk_preflight.sh:/t.sh:ro" \
            alpine:3.20 sh -c '
              apk add --no-cache bash >/dev/null &&
              DISK_PREFLIGHT_BIN=/lib.sh sh /t.sh
            '

      - name: Build frontend-v2 image
        env:
          BUILD_MIN_FREE_GB: "5"
        run: |
          . ./docker/shared/disk-preflight.sh
          mc_disk_preflight
          docker build -t mc-frontend-v2-test ./frontend-v2

      # PR #544 review (W1): this image was never built in CI, so the line
      # that could make the container PERMANENTLY unhealthy (installing the
      # healthcheck's tools) had never actually run — a healthcheck failing on
      # a missing binary is worse than the bug it looks for. Since the Debian
      # base (ADR-088 images step) websocat is the static release binary,
      # sha256-checked per arch; runner is ubuntu-latest (x86_64), the arm64
      # checksum is exercised on the production hardware at rollout.
      # NOTE: this proves the Dockerfile builds, not that this exact image
      # is the one running in production (that's built on arm64 hardware
      # and gets its own runtime/sabotage verification at rollout) — the
      # PR's review thread flagged conflating "CI green" with "runtime
      # proof" as exactly the kind of gap that let W1 slip through unnoticed.
      - name: Build cdp-browser image
        env:
          BUILD_MIN_FREE_GB: "5"
        run: |
          . ./docker/shared/disk-preflight.sh
          mc_disk_preflight
          docker build -t mc-cdp-browser-test ./docker/cdp-browser

      # WebGL must render and SURVIVE 4 GPU-process crashes, and healthchecks
      # must leave no zombies — with the flags + init read from
      # docker-compose.yml (live finding 02.10.: agent never saw its WebGL
      # scene; 71 716 zombies). Sabotage knobs documented in the script.
      - name: cdp-browser WebGL + zombie runtime test
        run: |
          python3 -c 'import yaml' 2>/dev/null || pip install --quiet pyyaml
          bash docker/cdp-browser/test_webgl.sh mc-cdp-browser-test docker-compose.yml

      # Sabotage tests for the healthcheck's WS leg against a mock CDP
      # server — run INSIDE the image built above (its websocat, wget,
      # timeout and python3), the exact runtime the healthcheck ships in —
      # see docker/cdp-browser/test_healthcheck.sh.
      - name: cdp-browser healthcheck sabotage tests
        run: |
          docker run --rm --entrypoint bash \
            -v "$PWD/docker/cdp-browser:/t:ro" \
            mc-cdp-browser-test /t/test_healthcheck.sh

      # Thin playwright-mcp image (exact npm version, WORKDIR /output for
      # named screenshots): it must build and report the pinned version.
      - name: Build playwright-mcp image
        env:
          BUILD_MIN_FREE_GB: "5"
        run: |
          . ./docker/shared/disk-preflight.sh
          mc_disk_preflight
          docker build -t mc-playwright-mcp-test ./docker/playwright-mcp
          docker run --rm --entrypoint playwright-mcp mc-playwright-mcp-test --version | grep -qx 'Version 0.0.83'
          test "$(docker run --rm --entrypoint pwd mc-playwright-mcp-test)" = /output
          # The entrypoint is the router: a stray flag must exit with 2, never
          # start a server (`timeout` would exit 124 — that is a failure too).
          rc=0; timeout 20 docker run --rm mc-playwright-mcp-test --version || rc=$?
          test "$rc" -eq 2

      # The router (one playwright-mcp child per browser session) — its node
      # tests run with the image's own node, against a fake playwright-mcp.
      - name: playwright-mcp router tests
        run: |
          timeout 180 docker run --rm --entrypoint node \
            -v "$PWD/docker/playwright-mcp:/t:ro" \
            mc-playwright-mcp-test --test --test-timeout=20000 /t/test/router.test.mjs

      # The agent images are node:alpine — BusyBox grep on musl, NOT GNU/BSD.
      # The fixtures in test_context_detect.sh catch most regressions on any
      # grep; this step exists for the NARROW class of divergences that only
      # show up on BusyBox/musl and that the host lane structurally cannot see
      # (review #487: e.g. `[:blank:]` semantics; measured against the fleet
      # binary BusyBox 1.36.1 / musl 1.2.5 extracted from node:22.11.0-alpine).
      - name: Bash lib smoke test on the BusyBox/musl runtime
        run: |
          docker run --rm \
            -v "$PWD/docker/mc-agent-base/lib/context-detect.sh:/lib.sh:ro" \
            -v "$PWD/backend/tests/test_context_detect.sh:/t.sh:ro" \
            alpine:3.20 sh -c 'apk add --no-cache bash >/dev/null && bash /t.sh /lib.sh'

      # Nachbehandlung wie in jedem lokalen Bau-Weg: Cache begrenzen statt
      # unbegrenzt wachsen lassen. Laeuft nur, wenn alle Bild-Builds oben
      # durch sind — ein Fehlschlag bricht den Job vorher ab und laesst den
      # Layer-Cache fuer den Retry stehen. BUILD_CACHE_KEEP_GB hier hoeher als
      # lokal (20), weil die Runner-Platte ohnehin fluechtig ist und die
      # Cache-Trefferquote dieses Jobs wichtiger ist als 15 GB Platz.
      - name: Bound the build cache
        env:
          BUILD_CACHE_KEEP_GB: "30"
        run: |
          . ./docker/shared/disk-preflight.sh
          mc_build_cache_cleanup

# Mission Control **A phone remote for coding agents on your own models — self-hosted, with approval gates.** Ask your lead agent from the couch, watch every edit land as a live diff, answer its questions with a tap — and keep the risky steps behind your approval. Runs on your hardware, prefers your local models, AGPL — with a **one-click model recipe for NVIDIA DGX Spark**. [![CI](https://github.com/argyelan-ai/mission-control/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/argyelan-ai/mission-control/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/argyelan-ai/mission-control?labelColor=1c1c1c)](https://github.com/argyelan-ai/mission-control/releases) [![License: AGPL-3.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-AGPL--3.0-informational?labelColor=1c1c1c)](LICENSE) [Spark recipe](#one-click-local-ai-on-dgx-spark) · [Install](#install) · [What it does](#what-it-does) · [Maturity](#what-is-stable-and-what-is-not) · [Docs](#docs) · [Roadmap](#where-its-going) · [Community](#community)
## One-click local AI on DGX Spark Pick a recipe on the **Runtimes** page and click **Install** — the recipe downloads the weights and sets up its engine while MC shows the live install log. For two-box recipes MC picks a free second box and wires it in. One click on **Start** switches a box (or a pair) to another recipe; a switch lock refuses it while the engine is still serving requests. | Recipe | Boxes | Engine | Measured on 2× DGX Spark | |---|---|---|---| | **GLM-5.3-Flash** · EXL3 4-bit · TensorFold | **2** (tensor parallel) | TensorFold | **62.6 tok/s** single stream · **211 tok/s** at 16 parallel · 1M context per request · prefill ~1,800 tok/s | This is the recipe MC ships today; more recipes are on the way and land in the same [catalog](backend/config/local-recipes.json). The recipe builds on other people's engines, quants and models — see [CREDITS](CREDITS.md). Note: the GLM recipe's default speculative drafter is licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (non-commercial); a licence-free drafter option exists. Numbers: our own benchmark (tokens counted from the API's `usage`, greedy, 512-token answers, on our own 2× DGX Spark pair, 08 Oct 2026); the same weights on the plain vLLM recipe reach 34.6 tok/s — the dedicated recipe is ~1.8× faster. **Catalog status:** this entry's `gb10_validated` flag is currently `false` — the catalog's own marker for "actually watched running on a GB10 box" is not yet set for this recipe, even though the numbers above come from a real run; if you install it and hit a mismatch, open an issue with your own numbers. How it works: [ADR-077](docs/decisions/077-rezept-modell-ein-startbefehl.md) · [Runtimes](docs/handbook/concepts/runtimes.md). ![Runtimes page: GPU boxes with the running model, context, speed, load and the Switch model button (demo data)](docs/assets/mc-runtimes.png) ## Why Coding agents are good enough to work while you are away from the desk. The tools around them are not: - **You can't see what they do.** A terminal on another machine is no use on a phone. MC turns the agent's work into a chat you can read anywhere: every tool call, every edit as a diff, every file it touched. - **You can't step in.** When an agent asks a question or wants approval, it waits — until you are back at a keyboard. In MC the question arrives as a card on your phone; you tap the answer and it carries on. - **Your code and prompts go to someone else's cloud.** MC is self-hosted. Point the local agent at your own GPU box (vLLM, LM Studio, Ollama, any OpenAI-compatible `/v1`) and that work never leaves your network. - **"Autonomous" usually means "unsupervised".** In MC, agents ask before risky actions — deploys, config changes, external posts — and your autonomy level decides whether that becomes a card you have to approve. MC also tells you exactly where the tokens went. ## What it does MC is built around **two fixed agents** and one chat to steer them: - a **lead agent** — your right hand, on Claude Code or on a local model; - a **local omp agent** — small jobs on your own GPU box, driven over ACP. ### Watch every edit as it happens Live tool output, a diff for each edit, file chips and the session cost — in the chat, on phone and desktop. The **Changes panel** lists what this chat changed, file by file, with **Revert**, **Commit** and **Open PR**. ![Desktop chat: the lead agent fixes a rounding bug; each edit shows as a diff and the Changes panel offers Revert, Commit and Open PR](docs/assets/mc-chat-desktop.png) The commit message is suggested by your local model when one is set up (otherwise MC writes a plain summary). The commit stays on your machine until you open the PR. ![Commit dialog with a commit message suggested by the local model](docs/assets/mc-chat-commit.png) ### Answer questions and approve plans from your phone

The local omp agent can stop and ask. Its questions arrive as **question cards**; in **plan mode** it writes a plan first and waits for *Approve*, *Refine* or *Cancel*. Screenshots taken by browser tools show up right on the tool card.

Phone use is **monitor and steer**: read, answer, approve, stop, send the next instruction. Full editing stays at the desk. MC installs as a home screen app (PWA manifest); it is not an offline app. ### Optional: talk to it Call your lead agent from the chat and give instructions by voice. This uses **OpenAI Realtime with your own API key** and has a **daily budget cap** (default 5 USD). It is off by default (`VOICE_LIVE_ENABLED`) and in preview ([ADR-091](docs/decisions/091-live-voice-in-the-chat.md), still *Proposed*). On a phone the browser only allows the microphone over HTTPS — see [Reverse proxy & remote access](docs/handbook/operations/reverse-proxy.md#https-with-your-own-certificate). ## Local first, honestly Your GPU boxes show up as runtimes with model, context, speed and load. For each agent you choose the runtime yourself; heads (preview) pre-select a local runtime when one exists. There is no automatic fallback from local to cloud yet. Not every coding tool runs on every model. The matrix shows what works today — and says **no**, with the reason, where it doesn't: ![Harness × runtime matrix: which coding tool runs on which kind of model, including the pairs that do not work](docs/assets/harness-matrix.svg) - **Claude Code runs on Claude.** It uses your own Claude Code login. Check your plan's terms for automated use. - **Local models run through omp or OpenClaude.** Claude Code on a local model is not offered for agents. - Switching an agent between runtimes goes through one switch service with a health check and rollback. Details: [Runtimes](docs/handbook/concepts/runtimes.md) · [Run agents on a local LLM](docs/handbook/howto/local-llm.md). ## Guardrails Agents ask MC before risky actions, and your settings decide what happens: - **Autonomy levels per action.** For each kind of action you choose *Auto* (done), *Notify* (done, and you are told) or *Approve* (a card that waits for you). Deploys, config changes and external posts are set to *Approve* by default. - **Approval cards.** An action set to *Approve* becomes a card in your inbox — one tap to allow or refuse, from the phone too. - **Honest limit:** this gate works because the agent asks. MC does not yet block an agent that skips the question, and the local omp agent runs its own tools without per-call prompts. The enforced gates today are the ADR gate below and your Git host's branch protection. - **ADR gate.** A pull request that changes a decision record cannot merge until you have approved that exact text. Editing it afterwards voids the approval. - **Git, not magic.** Work lands on branches and pull requests. Merges use the GitHub CLI (`gh pr merge --squash`) and respect your branch protection and merge queue. There is no merge button in the phone chat. ![Settings → Autonomy: Auto, Notify or Approve for each action type](docs/assets/mc-autonomy.png) ## See where the tokens go **Insights** shows tokens per day, the share that ran locally, where usage comes from (lead agent, omp agents, heads, you) and the local share per week. Costs are shown at list price, even on flat-rate plans, so you can compare. The chat's context ring shows the prompt cache hit rate. ![Insights with demo data: tokens per day, the share that ran locally, usage by source and local share per week](docs/assets/mc-insights.png) *The numbers in this picture are demo data.* ## What is stable and what is not MC is changing direction ([ADR-085](docs/decisions/085-head-per-job.md), [ADR-089](docs/decisions/089-lead-agent-with-hands.md), [ADR-090](docs/decisions/090-chat-as-remote-control.md)): away from a permanent fleet of named agents, towards one lead agent, one local agent and the chat as remote control. Here is where each part stands. | Status | What | How to get it | |---|---|---| | **Stable** | Core stack (boards, tasks, inbox, memory/vault, runtimes, insights, settings) · autonomy levels, approval cards, ADR gate · runtime switch with rollback | Default install | | **New (Oct 2026), live** | Chat with live diffs and Changes panel (Revert / Commit / Open PR) · question cards and plan mode for omp agents · tool screenshots. In daily use; the phone acceptance check and reliability work are still open ([ROADMAP](docs/ROADMAP.md)) | Default install | | **Preview, opt-in** | **Heads** — one short-lived coding session per job, in its own git worktree, ending in a PR and a run record | `HEADS_ENABLED=true` · **macOS host** (launchd + sandbox profile) | | **Preview, opt-in** | **Night shift** — "run tonight" jobs and a morning report | `NIGHT_SHIFT_ENABLED=true` · needs heads, so **macOS host** | | **Preview, opt-in** | **Live voice** in the chat ([ADR-091](docs/decisions/091-live-voice-in-the-chat.md)) | `VOICE_LIVE_ENABLED=true` + `OPENAI_API_KEY` · daily budget cap · HTTPS on the phone | | **Frozen** | The persistent agent fleet (dispatch, healers, group chat) · Skill Lab, ClawHub and plugin management | Still in the code, no new work; being removed step by step ([ROADMAP](docs/ROADMAP.md) E5) | **Fresh installs still start with the classic board.** The first-run wizard offers a demo board with a small demo crew of agents and sample tasks. That is the older picture of MC. The two-agent setup above is not created by the wizard yet — the [quickstart](docs/handbook/howto/quickstart.md) walks you through it. ![Home after the first run: the classic demo board with tasks in Inbox, In progress and Review](docs/assets/mc-home.png) ## Install **You need:** git, curl, openssl and Docker with Compose v2. The installer checks all of them at once and prints the exact command for anything that is missing — it never installs system packages on its own. ```bash # Debian / Ubuntu / Raspberry Pi OS sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y git curl openssl curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh && sudo usermod -aG docker "$USER" # then log out and in again # macOS: install Docker Desktop (and git via Xcode tools or Homebrew) ``` Then: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/argyelan-ai/mission-control/main/install.sh | bash ``` ![Installing Mission Control](docs/assets/install-demo.svg) The installer installs the **latest release** — code and prebuilt images of the same version (amd64 and arm64), so nothing has to be built. It writes `.env` with fresh secrets, starts the stack and prints the address to open. Developers who want `main` can pass `--channel edge` (built locally, not for everyday use). Update an install later from its folder with `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/argyelan-ai/mission-control/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --update` (never downgrades). Release rules: [ADR-092](docs/decisions/092-release-channels.md). **On a server or a Pi without a screen** the installer notices and asks whether you will open MC from another device. If yes, it creates the first admin account right there in the terminal (password hidden) and only then opens MC to your network — nobody else on the LAN can grab the admin account. Flags: `--remote`, `--public-host
`, `--local`. Prefer to keep MC private? Use an SSH tunnel (`ssh -L 8080:localhost:80 you@server`, then open `http://localhost:8080`) or [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com) (`tailscale serve --bg 80`, with `sudo` on Linux). Raspberry Pi notes (8 GB, SSD, memory cgroup): [docs/setup/raspberry-pi.md](docs/setup/raspberry-pi.md). On Linux, MC runs as your own user id (`PUID`/`PGID` in `.env`, set by the installer). If `/health` reports `degraded`, the message says what to fix. Run one-off commands as that user: `docker compose exec -u mcuser backend …`. After the first login the **setup wizard** opens by itself and stays until it is done. **After the install, no agent is running yet.** To get a lead agent and a local omp agent you can steer from the chat, follow **[Quickstart: install to your first remote-controlled agent](docs/handbook/howto/quickstart.md)**. ### Reach it from your phone Keep MC off the public internet. The easiest way to your phone is [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com): `tailscale serve --bg 80` (`sudo` on Linux) gives you an HTTPS address inside your tailnet without opening MC to the LAN — HTTPS is also what voice on the phone needs. Add MC to your home screen to use it as an app. Other options (LAN address, your own reverse proxy): [Reverse proxy & remote access](docs/handbook/operations/reverse-proxy.md). ## Platforms | Platform | Path | Notes | |---|---|---| | **macOS** | the one-liner | Everything, including heads and night shift (preview) | | **Linux server / NAS** | the one-liner | Core stack and Docker agents; no heads or host agents (they need macOS launchd) | | **Windows 10/11** | `.\setup.ps1` — sets up WSL2 + Docker, then runs the installer ([guide](docs/setup/windows.md)) | Same as Linux | | **Windows Server / company VM** | a small Linux VM next to your Windows VMs ([guide](docs/setup/windows.md#windows-server--company-hypervisors)) | Same as Linux | | **Runtipi** | [community app store](https://github.com/argyelan-ai/tipi-store) | Core stack only | | **Portainer** | [`deploy/catalogs/portainer-template.json`](deploy/catalogs/portainer-template.json) as an App Template source | Core stack only | | **Umbrel / CasaOS** | manifests prepared in [`deploy/catalogs/`](deploy/catalogs/), not submitted | — | Catalog installs run the core stack. Agents, heads and host-level extras need the full install. ## How it fits together ![How Mission Control works: phone → MC with lead agent and local omp agent, approval gates and insights → local or cloud models → your repo, branch and pull request](docs/assets/how-it-works.svg) - **Backend:** Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLModel, PostgreSQL 16, Redis 7, Qdrant, Alembic, server-sent events. - **Frontend:** Next.js 15 (App Router), TypeScript strict, Tailwind CSS v4, TanStack Query. - **Infrastructure:** Docker Compose, Caddy. The backend reaches Docker only through a filtering socket proxy. Full map and "where do I change what": [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). ## Docs | You want to… | Read | |---|---| | Find your way around `docs/` | [docs/README.md](docs/README.md) | | Get from install to a remote-controlled agent | [Quickstart](docs/handbook/howto/quickstart.md) | | Understand the lead agent, heads and the chat as remote control | [Heads and remote control](docs/handbook/concepts/heads-and-remote-control.md) | | Look things up | [Handbook](docs/handbook/index.md) · [FAQ](docs/handbook/faq.md) | | Connect GitHub | [docs/setup/github.md](docs/setup/github.md) | | Update or back up | [Updating](docs/setup/updating.md) · [Backup & restore](docs/handbook/operations/backup-restore.md) | | Know why things are built this way | [PRINCIPLES](docs/PRINCIPLES.md) · [90 decision records](docs/decisions/) | ## Where it's going No dates are promised; stages move when their acceptance check passes. Next in the chat: session list, resume and fork (P4), sending images, installing plugins, skills and MCP servers through an approval card. The lead agent's own merge and deploy gate is planned and not built yet. Full status: [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md). ## Built in the open - **90 decision records** in [`docs/decisions/`](docs/decisions/), each with its reason. Some are still *Proposed*; the status line says which. - **10,000+ backend and 3,000+ frontend tests**, and a CI pipeline that boots a fresh install end to end. - **Secure defaults:** ports bind to localhost until you opt in (the opt-in `voice` profile's LiveKit media ports are the exception), Docker only through a filtering socket proxy, secrets encrypted with Fernet. Reporting a vulnerability: [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Development: ```bash cd backend && python3.12 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate pip install -e ".[test]" && pytest -q # backend cd frontend-v2 && npm install && npm run test:run # frontend ``` `make help` lists the common entry points. Rules for contributors and coding agents: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). **Language note:** the project grew in a German-speaking home lab. Many ADRs and some code comments are German; the UI, README and setup are English (the UI also ships in German). ## Community - **Questions & ideas** — [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/argyelan-ai/mission-control/discussions) - **Bugs** — [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/argyelan-ai/mission-control/issues) - **Contributing** — [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) - **Code of Conduct** — [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) - **Security** — [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) ## Credits Mission Control's DGX Spark recipe builds on GLM-5.3-Flash by Z.ai, the EXL3 quantization format and ExLlamaV3 by turboderp, the TensorFold engine by ashhart, the DFlash2 drafter by Inco AI and the recipe work of Mia's AI Lab. MC drives the coding harnesses Claude Code, OpenClaude, omp, Hermes Agent, Kimi Code and Grok Build. Full list with licences and links: [CREDITS.md](./CREDITS.md). ## License AGPL-3.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Use it, self-host it, change it. If you distribute a modified version or offer it as a network service, share your changes under the same license. For commercial licensing beyond AGPL, contact the maintainer.

# Container logs are capped per service (30 MB max) — without this the
# json-file driver grows unbounded until the disk fills. Long-running
# self-hosted installs died silently on full disks otherwise.
x-logging: &default-logging
  driver: json-file
  options:
    max-size: "10m"
    max-file: "3"

services:
  db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    # Docker Desktop defaults StopTimeout to 1s when a service doesn't set
    # this explicitly (measured, not assumed — see architecture session
    # 2026-09-14). Postgres under SIGKILL never runs a clean checkpoint, it
    # just crash-recovers on the next start. 60s gives it real headroom to
    # shut down cleanly on every `docker stop`/recreate.
    stop_grace_period: 60s
    logging: *default-logging
    volumes:
      - mc_postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./pg_hba.conf:/pg_hba_custom.conf:ro
    command: ["postgres", "-c", "hba_file=/pg_hba_custom.conf"]
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: mc
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_DB: mission_control
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:5432:5432"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U mc"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    # Same Docker-Desktop default gap as db (1s without this line). AOF is on
    # (--appendonly yes --appendfsync everysec): on SIGTERM redis-server finishes
    # writing to the AOF file and closes it cleanly; on SIGKILL that in-flight
    # write — and the clean close — is lost. 30s is generous headroom for that
    # flush, not a full minute like db: there's no checkpoint/WAL replay to wait
    # out, just a bounded fsync.
    stop_grace_period: 30s
    logging: *default-logging
    command: redis-server --requirepass ${REDIS_PASSWORD} --appendonly yes --appendfsync everysec
    volumes:
      - mc_redis_data:/data
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:6379:6379"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "-a", "${REDIS_PASSWORD}", "ping"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  # Docker-API-Filter (Hardening): das Backend spricht NIE direkt mit
  # /var/run/docker.sock, sondern via DOCKER_HOST mit diesem Proxy. Der
  # Proxy whitelistet nur die API-Pfade, die MC braucht (Container-
  # Lifecycle, exec fuer tmux-respawn, images/networks/volumes fuer
  # compose up). Swarm/Secrets/Build/System bleiben geblockt — ein
  # kompromittiertes Backend kann den Host nicht via Docker uebernehmen.
  docker-socket-proxy:
    image: tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy:v0.4.2
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *default-logging
    environment:
      CONTAINERS: 1   # inspect/list + lifecycle (mit POST)
      IMAGES: 1       # compose up prueft Images
      NETWORKS: 1     # compose verbindet Agent-Container
      VOLUMES: 1      # compose inspiziert benannte Volumes
      EXEC: 1         # tmux respawn-window / Sessions-Terminal
      INFO: 1         # docker compose ruft /info
      POST: 1         # Schreiboperationen generell (gefiltert durch obige)
      ALLOW_START: 1
      ALLOW_STOP: 1
      ALLOW_RESTARTS: 1
      BUILD: 0        # Image-Builds laufen auf dem Host, nie im Backend
      SWARM: 0
      SYSTEM: 0
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    # Bewusst KEIN ports:-Eintrag — nur intern erreichbar.

  backend:
    # Offizielles Image (GHCR) — `docker compose pull` holt es; wenn es lokal
    # fehlt UND nicht pullbar ist, greift der build:-Fallback (pull_policy
    # default 'build' bei vorhandener build:-Sektion). MC_IMAGE_TAG pinnt
    # Versionen (default latest).
    image: ghcr.io/argyelan-ai/mc-backend:${MC_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    build: ./backend
    restart: unless-stopped
    # tini as PID 1 instead of docker-entrypoint.sh/uvicorn: the kernel drops
    # any signal PID 1 has no handler for, so a stop during migrations or the
    # import phase used to wait the full stop_grace_period and end in SIGKILL.
    # tini forwards SIGTERM to a normal child (see the mc-worker comment).
    init: true
    # Same Docker-Desktop default gap as db/caddy (1s without this line) —
    # 20s gives in-flight requests and the FastAPI shutdown hooks room to
    # finish instead of a hard SIGKILL mid-request.
    stop_grace_period: 20s
    logging: *default-logging
    networks:
      - default
      - cdpnet
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      docker-socket-proxy:
        condition: service_started
    environment:
      # Architektur E Teil 2: Hintergrund-Dienste (Scheduler/Watchdog/Task-
      # Runner/Telegram-/Slack-Inbound/Vault-Watcher) laufen IM mc-worker-
      # Container unten — die API bleibt schlank und beantwortet nur Requests.
      # Genau EIN Prozess traegt den Flag true (Worker); config.py-Default
      # bleibt True (Rueckweg fuer compose-freie Installs).
      ENABLE_BACKGROUND_SERVICES: "false"
      # Head launcher switch (docs/specs/head-launcher.md) — off unless set in .env
      HEADS_ENABLED: ${HEADS_ENABLED:-false}
      # Head watchdog: stop after N min without progress; hard limit = emergency brake
      HEADS_NO_PROGRESS_MIN: ${HEADS_NO_PROGRESS_MIN:-20}
      HEADS_HARD_LIMIT_LOCAL_S: ${HEADS_HARD_LIMIT_LOCAL_S:-28800}
      HEADS_HARD_LIMIT_CLOUD_S: ${HEADS_HARD_LIMIT_CLOUD_S:-7200}
      # Konsument ist backend/app/routers/browser_live.py — ein Router, also
      # der API-Prozess. War auf main gesetzt und wurde beim Teil-2-Umbau
      # still ersetzt statt ergaenzt (Rex-Review PR #500, Blocker B4):
      # wiederhergestellt, Flag-Zeile darueber ergaenzt, nicht ersetzt.
      CDP_BROWSER_URL: http://172.30.99.10:9223
      # Plattenplatz: Bau-Preflight und Waechter. Wie bei Telegram muss JEDE
      # Variable hier einzeln stehen — es gibt keine env_file-Direktive, die
      # .env allein erreicht den Container nicht. Der Waechter laeuft im
      # Worker, die Preflight-Pfade im API-Prozess: beide brauchen die Werte.
      BUILD_MIN_FREE_GB: ${BUILD_MIN_FREE_GB:-15}
      BUILD_CACHE_KEEP_GB: ${BUILD_CACHE_KEEP_GB:-20}
      DISK_WATCHDOG_PERCENT: ${DISK_WATCHDOG_PERCENT:-95}
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql+asyncpg://mc:${DB_PASSWORD}@db:5432/mission_control
      REDIS_URL: redis://:${REDIS_PASSWORD}@redis:6379/0
      AUTH_MODE: local
      LOCAL_AUTH_TOKEN: ${LOCAL_AUTH_TOKEN}
      JWT_SECRET_KEY: ${JWT_SECRET_KEY:-change-me-in-production}
      # User session lifetime; override in .env (e.g. 43200 = 30 days on a Tailscale-only install)
      JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES: ${JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES:-480}
      # Streams (SSE/WebSocket) open with single-use tickets (?ticket=). The
      # old login token in the URL (?token=) leaks into proxy logs and is off;
      # true re-enables it for one transition release only.
      ALLOW_QUERY_TOKEN_AUTH: ${ALLOW_QUERY_TOKEN_AUTH:-false}
      STREAM_TICKET_TTL_SECONDS: ${STREAM_TICKET_TTL_SECONDS:-60}
      SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY: ${SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY:-}
      DISCORD_WEBHOOK_OPS: ${DISCORD_WEBHOOK_OPS:-}
      DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN: ${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN:-}
      DISCORD_GUILD_ID: ${DISCORD_GUILD_ID:-}
      DISCORD_CATEGORY_ID: ${DISCORD_CATEGORY_ID:-}
      TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN: ${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN:-}
      TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID: ${TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID:-}
      TELEGRAM_REPORTS_BOT_TOKEN: ${TELEGRAM_REPORTS_BOT_TOKEN:-}
      TELEGRAM_REPORTS_CHAT_ID: ${TELEGRAM_REPORTS_CHAT_ID:-}
      # Jarvis Telegram-Inbound (ADR-061): mobiler Jarvis via Telegram Text/Voice.
      # Default aus → Verhalten unveraendert (nur Approval-URL-Buttons).
      # Team-Chat: Telegram-Themen <-> MC-Threads (P2.2-P2.4). Ohne diese
      # Zeile erreicht das Flag den Container nie — die .env allein reicht
      # nicht, weil hier jede Telegram-Variable einzeln durchgereicht wird.
      TELEGRAM_TEAM_CHAT_ENABLED: ${TELEGRAM_TEAM_CHAT_ENABLED:-false}
      # Kanal-Schalter des Team-Chats (ADR-072): Komma-Liste der aktiven
      # Kanaele, z.B. "telegram", "slack" oder "telegram,slack". Leer =
      # keine explizite Auswahl → jeder registrierte Kanal darf laufen,
      # sofern sein eigener Schalter an ist (heutiges Verhalten).
      CHAT_CHANNELS: ${CHAT_CHANNELS:-}
      # Slack-Team-Chat (ADR-072). Wie bei Telegram muss JEDE Variable hier
      # einzeln stehen — die .env allein erreicht den Container nicht. Die
      # beiden Slack-TOKEN gehoeren bewusst NICHT hierher: sie liegen
      # verschluesselt in der secrets-Tabelle (ADR-033).
      SLACK_TEAM_CHAT_ENABLED: ${SLACK_TEAM_CHAT_ENABLED:-false}
      SLACK_DEFAULT_CHANNEL: ${SLACK_DEFAULT_CHANNEL:-}
      # Reports-Kanal (#mc-reports) fuer den OperatorReports-Adapter — leer =
      # Slack-Reports aus, Telegram-Bot bleibt alleiniger Report-Weg.
      SLACK_REPORTS_CHANNEL: ${SLACK_REPORTS_CHANNEL:-}
      # Cap fuer Dateien, die der Operator ueber Slack an MC schickt
      # (Datei-Ingest -> References). Default 25 MB.
      SLACK_FILE_INGEST_MAX_BYTES: ${SLACK_FILE_INGEST_MAX_BYTES:-26214400}
      # Approvals-Kanal (#mc-approvals) — leer = keine Slack-Approvals,
      # Telegram-Buttons laufen unabhaengig weiter (Fan-out).
      SLACK_APPROVALS_CHANNEL: ${SLACK_APPROVALS_CHANNEL:-}
      JARVIS_TELEGRAM_ENABLED: ${JARVIS_TELEGRAM_ENABLED:-false}
      OPENAI_API_KEY: ${OPENAI_API_KEY:-}
      JARVIS_TEXT_MODEL: ${JARVIS_TEXT_MODEL:-gpt-4o-mini}
      JARVIS_STT_MODEL: ${JARVIS_STT_MODEL:-gpt-4o-mini-transcribe}
      # Local/self-hosted STT endpoint (scripts/stt-server). Every backend env
      # var must be mapped HERE explicitly — the setting existed in config.py
      # first and silently never reached the container (found live 2026-07-30:
      # printenv came back empty while the unit tests were all green).
      STT_BASE_URL: ${STT_BASE_URL:-}
      STT_MODEL: ${STT_MODEL:-}
      # Agent bootstrap auth (PR #404 Rex review, HIGH): agents fetch their
      # tokens at startup via Bearer INTERNAL_BOOTSTRAP_SECRET
      # (docker/.env.shared via start-all.sh, written by setup.sh into .env).
      # Like every backend var, it must be mapped HERE explicitly — the .env
      # alone never reaches the container (same trap as STT_BASE_URL above,
      # found live 2026-07-30). Empty in a dev .env = endpoint stays open,
      # exactly like local dev; production (ENVIRONMENT=production) refuses
      # to boot without it (config.py::validate_boot_secrets).
      INTERNAL_BOOTSTRAP_SECRET: ${INTERNAL_BOOTSTRAP_SECRET:-}
      # Jarvis Intelligence (ADR-062): frontier delegation (ask_frontier) + the
      # daily morning briefing job. Empty model → jarvis_core default (gpt-5.5).
      # ask_frontier is off by default (per-request cost); the briefing job has
      # its own gate below and is unaffected.
      JARVIS_FRONTIER_MODEL: ${JARVIS_FRONTIER_MODEL:-}
      JARVIS_FRONTIER_ENABLED: ${JARVIS_FRONTIER_ENABLED:-false}
      JARVIS_BRIEFING_ENABLED: ${JARVIS_BRIEFING_ENABLED:-false}
      JARVIS_BRIEFING_HOUR: ${JARVIS_BRIEFING_HOUR:-06:30}
      # Jarvis-Agent-Token: der Brain fuehrt Tool-Calls ueber den agent-scoped
      # API-Pfad aus (kein Auth-Bypass), derselbe Token wie der voice_worker.
      JARVIS_AGENT_TOKEN: ${JARVIS_AGENT_TOKEN:-}
      # Wer "der Operator" ist: liefert den Anzeigenamen fuer die Anrede
      # (users.preferred_name) und ist der zweite, vom Scope unabhaengige
      # Schalter fuer die Operator-Proxy-Endpoints. Leer => Jarvis bleibt bei
      # der neutralen Anrede, Proxy-Endpoints antworten 503.
      JARVIS_OPERATOR_USER_ID: ${JARVIS_OPERATOR_USER_ID:-}
      # Sprach-Stimme je Anbieter (ADR-082): resolve_voice_config() liest diese
      # zwei Variablen aus der Backend-Env, NICHT aus der voice-worker-Env — die
      # Bindung entscheidet WELCHER Anbieter aktiv ist, die Stimme ist dessen
      # eigene Einstellung. Getrennt weil die Stimmnamen pro Anbieter disjunkt
      # sind ("marin" bei OpenAI, "ara" bei xAI) — eine geteilte Variable
      # zerlegte den jeweils inaktiven Arm.
      VOICE_OPENAI_VOICE_ID: ${VOICE_OPENAI_VOICE_ID:-}
      VOICE_XAI_VOICE_ID: ${VOICE_XAI_VOICE_ID:-}
      # Live voice in the chat (ADR-091 draft): off unless set; needs
      # OPENAI_API_KEY too. Mapped for backend AND mc-worker (one Settings).
      VOICE_LIVE_ENABLED: ${VOICE_LIVE_ENABLED:-false}
      VOICE_LIVE_MODEL: ${VOICE_LIVE_MODEL:-gpt-realtime-2.1}
      VOICE_LIVE_VOICE: ${VOICE_LIVE_VOICE:-marin}
      VOICE_LIVE_PRICE_AUDIO_IN_PER_M: ${VOICE_LIVE_PRICE_AUDIO_IN_PER_M:-32.0}
      VOICE_LIVE_PRICE_AUDIO_OUT_PER_M: ${VOICE_LIVE_PRICE_AUDIO_OUT_PER_M:-64.0}
      VOICE_LIVE_PRICE_CACHED_IN_PER_M: ${VOICE_LIVE_PRICE_CACHED_IN_PER_M:-0.40}
      VOICE_LIVE_PRICE_TEXT_IN_PER_M: ${VOICE_LIVE_PRICE_TEXT_IN_PER_M:-4.0}
      VOICE_LIVE_PRICE_TEXT_OUT_PER_M: ${VOICE_LIVE_PRICE_TEXT_OUT_PER_M:-24.0}
      VOICE_LIVE_IDLE_HANGUP_S: ${VOICE_LIVE_IDLE_HANGUP_S:-120}
      VOICE_LIVE_IDLE_WARN_S: ${VOICE_LIVE_IDLE_WARN_S:-15}
      VOICE_LIVE_MAX_CALL_S: ${VOICE_LIVE_MAX_CALL_S:-1200}
      VOICE_LIVE_DAILY_BUDGET_USD: ${VOICE_LIVE_DAILY_BUDGET_USD:-5.0}
      VOICE_LIVE_BUDGET_TZ: ${VOICE_LIVE_BUDGET_TZ:-Europe/Zurich}
      # Self-Call-Basis fuer den geteilten mc_client (Brain laeuft IM Backend).
      MC_BACKEND_URL: http://localhost:8000
      MC_BASE_URL: ${MC_BASE_URL:-http://localhost}
      # Adresse(n) fuer den node-agent-Install-Einzeiler (Geraete -> "Geraet
      # hinzufuegen"); kommagetrennt = eine Zeile je Netz (Tailscale + LAN).
      # Ohne Passthrough las das Backend die Variable nie (Live-Fund 03.09.2026).
      MC_NODE_AGENT_BASE_URL: ${MC_NODE_AGENT_BASE_URL:-}
      # Operator identity (see .env.example)
      OPERATOR_NAME: ${OPERATOR_NAME:-Operator}
      HOST_SSH_USER: ${HOST_SSH_USER:-}
      # Externally reachable host (Tailscale IP / LAN / DNS) — CORS allowlist +
      # phone-test deep links (ADR-040, replaces hardcoded IPs in product code).
      PUBLIC_HOST: ${PUBLIC_HOST:-}
      EXTRA_CORS_ORIGINS: ${EXTRA_CORS_ORIGINS:-}
      # ADR-084: fleet-wide omp driver default (acp | native). ACP is a
      # harness property — this one knob rolls the WHOLE fleet back to the
      # native TUI driver, no agent name lists. Without this passthrough the
      # .env key never reaches the backend container (same trap as
      # STT_BASE_URL above).
      OMP_DRIVER_DEFAULT: ${OMP_DRIVER_DEFAULT:-acp}
      RECOVERY_TIER2_SKIP_AGENT_SLUGS: ${RECOVERY_TIER2_SKIP_AGENT_SLUGS:-}
      # Treiber der hermes-bridge auf dem Host (native | acp). Gleiche Falle:
      # ohne Passthrough kaeme der .env-Schluessel nie im Container an, und
      # Hermes' Chat bliebe stumm (docs/specs/chat-over-acp.md).
      HERMES_DRIVER: ${HERMES_DRIVER:-native}
      GH_TOKEN: ${GH_TOKEN:-}
      # Kill-switch: false = legacy single-session dispatch (see ADR-002).
      # NOTE: still live in 7 call sites — CLAUDE.md's "obsolete" note is stale.
      USE_SUBAGENT_DISPATCH: ${USE_SUBAGENT_DISPATCH:-true}
      # GitHub owner (user/org) for the agent git workflow (repos, PRs).
      GITHUB_OWNER: ${GITHUB_OWNER:-}
      # Repo-name prefixes the visibility monitor keeps private.
      MC_OWNED_REPO_PREFIXES: ${MC_OWNED_REPO_PREFIXES:-mc-,mc-task-,t2-}
      # Voice-Agent: LiveKit-Token-Signing braucht api_key + secret separat.
      # PUBLIC_URL = was der Browser-Client erreicht (vs internal ws://livekit:7880).
      LIVEKIT_API_KEY: ${LIVEKIT_API_KEY:-}
      LIVEKIT_API_SECRET: ${LIVEKIT_API_SECRET:-}
      # LIVEKIT_PUBLIC_URL leer = dynamic derivation aus Request-Origin
      # (siehe routers/voice.py:_derive_ws_url). Caddy proxiert /livekit-signal.
      LIVEKIT_PUBLIC_URL: ${LIVEKIT_PUBLIC_URL:-}
      # ADR-023 ultrareview / ADR-006 SSoT: nur `.env`-Vars mit Defaults,
      # keine Hardcodes in compose. `.env.example` dokumentiert die Keys.
      SPARK_EMBEDDING_URL: ${SPARK_EMBEDDING_URL:-}
      SPARK_EMBEDDING_MODEL: ${SPARK_EMBEDDING_MODEL:-text-embedding-nomic-embed-text-v1.5}
      # MC's own AI functions (docs/setup/ai-providers.md) — without this
      # passthrough the documented AI_* .env block never reaches the container.
      AI_EMBEDDINGS_PROVIDER: ${AI_EMBEDDINGS_PROVIDER:-spark}
      AI_EMBEDDINGS_URL: ${AI_EMBEDDINGS_URL:-}
      AI_EMBEDDINGS_MODEL: ${AI_EMBEDDINGS_MODEL:-}
      AI_EMBEDDINGS_CLOUD_URL: ${AI_EMBEDDINGS_CLOUD_URL:-}
      AI_EMBEDDINGS_CLOUD_MODEL: ${AI_EMBEDDINGS_CLOUD_MODEL:-}
      AI_INSIGHTS_PROVIDER: ${AI_INSIGHTS_PROVIDER:-spark}
      AI_INSIGHTS_MODEL: ${AI_INSIGHTS_MODEL:-}
      SPARK_LLM_URL: ${SPARK_LLM_URL:-http://192.0.2.10:8000/v1}
      DGX_SSH_HOST: ${DGX_SSH_HOST:-}
      DGX_SSH_USER: ${DGX_SSH_USER:-}
      DGX_SSH_KEY_PATH: ${DGX_SSH_KEY_PATH:-/home/mcuser/.ssh/id_rsa}
      ENABLE_DISPATCH_GATING: ${ENABLE_DISPATCH_GATING:-false}
      LEAD_AUTO_ASSIGN_NEW_TASKS: ${LEAD_AUTO_ASSIGN_NEW_TASKS:-}
      STRUCTURED_INTAKE_ENABLED: ${STRUCTURED_INTAKE_ENABLED:-false}
      ENABLE_PROMOTE_ORCHESTRATOR: ${ENABLE_PROMOTE_ORCHESTRATOR:-false}
      ENVIRONMENT: production
      # Docker-Zugriff ausschliesslich ueber den gefilterten Socket-Proxy
      # (Service oben). Der docker-CLI + compose respektieren DOCKER_HOST;
      # alle Backend-Subprozesse erben os.environ.
      DOCKER_HOST: tcp://docker-socket-proxy:2375
      HOME_HOST: ${HOME}
      # Absolute host path of this repo checkout — the Python side
      # (settings.mc_repo_path: force-recreate, runtime-switch, compose
      # renderer) needs it INSIDE the container; the volume interpolation
      # below only resolves it on the host.
      MC_REPO_PATH: ${MC_REPO_PATH:-${HOME}/Workspace/Projects/mission-control}
      # Agent image naming for the compose renderer (see .env.example).
      # Default = published GHCR images (since v0.2.0); "" = bare local names.
      MC_AGENT_IMAGE_PREFIX: ${MC_AGENT_IMAGE_PREFIX-ghcr.io/argyelan-ai/}
      MC_AGENT_IMAGE_TAG: ${MC_AGENT_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
      # Host UID — used by cli_terminal._user_default_tmux_socket() to build the
      # tmux socket path (/tmp/tmux-<uid>/default) that the host-pty-bridge will
      # attach to. Without this, getuid() returns 1000 (the in-container user)
      # and the bridge fails with "no such file or directory" on the host.
      HOST_UID: ${HOST_UID:-502}
      # Run as the host user's uid/gid so the ~/.mc bind mount is writable on
      # Linux (docker-entrypoint.sh remaps mcuser, then drops root). setup.sh
      # fills both from `id -u`/`id -g` on Linux. Empty = mcuser 1000 as before
      # (macOS/Windows Docker Desktop map uids themselves).
      PUID: ${PUID:-}
      PGID: ${PGID:-}
      # cli-bridge host helper auth (docs/setup/cli-bridge-auth.md). Empty =
      # read ~/.mc/secrets/cli-bridge.token through the ~/.mc mount below.
      CLI_BRIDGE_TOKEN: ${CLI_BRIDGE_TOKEN:-}
      CLI_BRIDGE_TOKEN_FILE: ${CLI_BRIDGE_TOKEN_FILE:-}
      # ADR-022: MC-Home unter ~/.mc/. Stage-2-Entkopplung (2026-06-01): aller
      # Backend-Code referenziert jetzt direkt ~/.mc/...; der Legacy ~/.openclaw
      # Mount wurde entfernt (Host-Symlinks bleiben bis Stage 3 bestehen).
      MC_MCP_REGISTRY_DIR: ${HOME}/.mc/mcp-servers
      MC_AGENTS_ROOT: ${HOME}/.mc/agents
    volumes:
      - ${HOME}/.mc:${HOME}/.mc
      # Host-specific extras (SSH keys for remote runtimes, free-code sandbox
      # mounts, custom Caddyfile) belong in docker-compose.override.yml —
      # see docker-compose.override.example.yml. Do NOT hardcode them here.
      # Deliverables-Mount: Agents schreiben unter /deliverables/<task_id>/
      # (im Agent-Container) — der Host-Pfad ist ~/.mc/deliverables/<slug>/.
      # Backend mountet alle Agent-Slugs zusammengefasst unter /deliverables/
      # damit FileResponse den path-Wert aus der DB direkt aufloesen kann.
      - ${HOME}/.mc/deliverables:/deliverables:ro
      # Shared Deliverables fuer mc-playwright Screenshots. rw seit PR3
      # (Benchmark Studio): der Orchestrator schreibt bench-<id>/<label>/
      # index.html hierher, damit mc-playwright /record es laden kann
      # (Praezedenz: mcp-screenshots-Mount wurde am 05.07. ro->rw geflippt).
      - mc_shared_deliverables:/shared-deliverables
      # MCP Screenshots (Microsoft Playwright MCP Sidecar) — read-only fuer
      # Backend's `mc deliverable from-mcp` Validierung + FileResponse.
      # rw seit 05.07.: Task-Delete räumt /shared-mcp/<task_id>/ mit
      # (E2E-Videos/Screenshots, services/mcp_media_cleanup.py) — vorher ro.
      - ${HOME}/.mc/mcp-screenshots:/shared-mcp
      # Host-agent integration sources (Boss ~/.claude transcripts, Grok
      # ~/.grok, Hermes ~/.hermes/state.db for the token harvester / model
      # catalog) are OPT-IN mounts: a fresh install has none of these tools,
      # and Docker would create the missing paths as empty root-owned
      # directories in $HOME. If you run host agents, copy the block from
      # docker-compose.override.example.yml (it documents the sharp edges:
      # Grok auth.json inode rotation, Hermes -wal/-shm corruption risk).
      # Templates als Live-Mount — Aenderungen an *.j2 werden vom
      # template_renderer.py (FileSystemLoader mit auto_reload) sofort
      # aufgenommen. Kein Backend-Rebuild mehr bei Template-Aenderungen.
      - ./backend/templates:/app/templates:ro
      # docker/ Live-Mount fuer compose_renderer.py — der Renderer liest +
      # schreibt docker-compose.agents.yml beim Cross-Image Runtime-Switch.
      # Mount unter dem absoluten Host-Pfad, weil der Code via HOME_HOST den
      # gleichen Pfad in-container erwartet (ADR-027 / Phase 15).
      # MC_REPO_PATH = absolute host path of this repo checkout (set by setup.sh).
      - ./docker:${MC_REPO_PATH:-${HOME}/Workspace/Projects/mission-control}/docker:rw
      # docker-compose.yml + .env fuer `docker compose -f ... up -d
      # --force-recreate` Cross-Image Switches (ADR-027 / Phase 15).
      - ./docker-compose.yml:${MC_REPO_PATH:-${HOME}/Workspace/Projects/mission-control}/docker-compose.yml:ro
      - ./.env:${MC_REPO_PATH:-${HOME}/Workspace/Projects/mission-control}/.env:ro
      # Shared Jarvis package (ADR-061). The backend build context is ./backend
      # (also the GHCR image path), so jarvis_core — which lives at the repo
      # root — is provided as a live mount rather than baked in, matching the
      # ./backend/templates and ./docker live-mount convention above. The
      # Telegram-inbound import of jarvis_core is lazy + feature-gated, so a
      # pure image run without this mount is unaffected (feature stays off).
      - ./jarvis_core:/app/jarvis_core:ro
      # mc-node-agent Quelle (Fleet & Rezepte v2, Phase 1) — wie jarvis_core
      # oben: GET /api/v1/nodes/agent-script (routers/nodes.py) liefert die
      # Kopie DIESER laufenden Instanz, damit der Agent einer gepaarten Box
      # immer zur API passt, mit der er redet. Fehlt der Mount → 404,
      # feature-gated wie jarvis_core.
      # VERZEICHNIS statt Einzeldatei (P2, 02.09.2026): ein Einzeldatei-
      # Bind-Mount hängt am Inode; `git checkout` im Deploy-Worktree schreibt
      # die Datei neu und der Mount zeigte danach ins Leere (404, belegt
      # 01.09.2026). Ein Verzeichnis löst den Namen bei jedem Zugriff neu auf.
      - ./scripts/node-agent:/app/scripts/node-agent:ro
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8000:8000"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "python -c \"import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8000/health')\""]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      # First boot on slow hardware (Raspberry Pi, SD card): migrations and
      # the first vector-store collections run past a minute. Failed probes
      # inside start_period do not count, and the first good probe marks the
      # backend healthy at once — fast machines are not slowed down.
      start_period: 300s

  # Architektur E Teil 2: eigener Hintergrund-Dienst-Container. Gleiches
  # Image wie die API (backend), aber Einstiegspunkt `python -m app.worker`
  # statt uvicorn — kein HTTP-Port, dafuer Scheduler/Watchdog/Task-Runner/
  # Telegram-/Slack-Inbound/Vault-Watcher/-Compactor/Lint-Cron.
  # Genau EIN Prozess mit ENABLE_BACKGROUND_SERVICES=true (hier); die API
  # oben laeuft mit false. Siehe ~/.claude/skills/mc-deploy/SKILL.md.
  mc-worker:
    image: ghcr.io/argyelan-ai/mc-backend:${MC_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    build: ./backend
    # Worker haengt an der API: Seeds/Migrationen (docker-entrypoint.sh) und
    # der Settings-Patchlauf (channel/ai-provider overrides) sollen zuerst
    # gelaufen sein, bevor der Worker dieselben idempotenten Seeds anstoesst.
    entrypoint: ["/docker-entrypoint.sh"]
    command: ["python", "-m", "app.worker"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    # tini (docker-init) as PID 1. Without it the entrypoint and then
    # `python -m app.worker` ARE PID 1, and the kernel drops every signal
    # PID 1 has no handler for (man 7 pid_namespaces). The worker only
    # installs its SIGTERM handler after its imports (app/worker.py, #509),
    # so `docker stop` during alembic or the import phase waited the full
    # 30s below and ended in SIGKILL (exit 137), measured live after #509.
    # With tini the worker is a normal child: SIGTERM before the handler
    # exists ends it at once (default action), afterwards the graceful path
    # runs. Nothing in the image relies on being PID 1.
    init: true
    # W4 (11.09.2026, Incident Deploy #504): Docker default is 10s. The
    # worker's SIGTERM handler awaits stop_vault_services() + 17
    # sequential service .stop() calls (app/worker.py, app/background.py)
    # before SchedulerService.stop() — the last of the chain — can delete
    # its Redis lock. Under 10s that chain didn't finish before SIGKILL,
    # so the lock only healed via its 120s TTL. 30s gives the shutdown
    # chain realistic headroom; per-service duration is now logged
    # (app/background.py:_timed_stop) so a future slow step is visible
    # instead of just "scheduler lock stuck again".
    stop_grace_period: 30s
    logging: *default-logging
    depends_on:
      backend:
        condition: service_healthy
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
      docker-socket-proxy:
        condition: service_started
    environment:
      ENABLE_BACKGROUND_SERVICES: "true"
      # Head launcher switch (docs/specs/head-launcher.md) — off unless set in .env
      HEADS_ENABLED: ${HEADS_ENABLED:-false}
      # Head watchdog: stop after N min without progress; hard limit = emergency brake
      HEADS_NO_PROGRESS_MIN: ${HEADS_NO_PROGRESS_MIN:-20}
      HEADS_HARD_LIMIT_LOCAL_S: ${HEADS_HARD_LIMIT_LOCAL_S:-28800}
      HEADS_HARD_LIMIT_CLOUD_S: ${HEADS_HARD_LIMIT_CLOUD_S:-7200}
      # W2 (Rex-Review PR #500): Migrationen macht der backend-Container
      # (depends_on: backend: service_healthy stellt die Reihenfolge sicher).
      # Ein zweiter alembic-Lauf hier waere ein Migrations-Wettlauf gegen
      # genau die Invariante, die der entrypoint-Kommentar behauptet
      # ("genau ein Backend-Container").
      MC_SKIP_MIGRATIONS: "1"
      # Identische Env wie backend (dieselbe settings-Factory, dieselben
      # Overrides) — jede Abweichung driftet API- und Worker-Sicht auseinander.
      # AUSNAHME CDP_BROWSER_URL (Rex-Review PR #500, Blocker B4): der einzige
      # Konsument (routers/browser_live.py) laeuft im API-Prozess; der Worker
      # haengt nur am default-Netz (kein cdpnet), die fixe cdpnet-IP
      # 172.30.99.10 waere hier unerreichbar. Bewusst nicht kopiert.
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql+asyncpg://mc:${DB_PASSWORD}@db:5432/mission_control
      REDIS_URL: redis://:${REDIS_PASSWORD}@redis:6379/0
      AUTH_MODE: local
      LOCAL_AUTH_TOKEN: ${LOCAL_AUTH_TOKEN}
      JWT_SECRET_KEY: ${JWT_SECRET_KEY:-change-me-in-production}
      JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES: ${JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES:-480}
      SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY: ${SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY:-}
      # Plattenplatz: der Waechter laeuft hier (ENABLE_BACKGROUND_SERVICES),
      # also muss mindestens DISK_WATCHDOG_PERCENT hier stehen — sonst laeuft
      # er mit dem falschen Wert. Die beiden Bau-Schwellen stehen mit, weil
      # der Regelkommentar oben "identische Env" verlangt und der
      # Cache-Cleanup auch aus Worker-Kontext erreichbar ist.
      BUILD_MIN_FREE_GB: ${BUILD_MIN_FREE_GB:-15}
      BUILD_CACHE_KEEP_GB: ${BUILD_CACHE_KEEP_GB:-20}
      DISK_WATCHDOG_PERCENT: ${DISK_WATCHDOG_PERCENT:-95}
      DISCORD_WEBHOOK_OPS: ${DISCORD_WEBHOOK_OPS:-}
      DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN: ${DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN:-}
      DISCORD_GUILD_ID: ${DISCORD_GUILD_ID:-}
      DISCORD_CATEGORY_ID: ${DISCORD_CATEGORY_ID:-}
      TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN: ${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN:-}
      TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID: ${TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID:-}
      TELEGRAM_REPORTS_BOT_TOKEN: ${TELEGRAM_REPORTS_BOT_TOKEN:-}
      TELEGRAM_REPORTS_CHAT_ID: ${TELEGRAM_REPORTS_CHAT_ID:-}
      TELEGRAM_TEAM_CHAT_ENABLED: ${TELEGRAM_TEAM_CHAT_ENABLED:-false}
      CHAT_CHANNELS: ${CHAT_CHANNELS:-}
      SLACK_TEAM_CHAT_ENABLED: ${SLACK_TEAM_CHAT_ENABLED:-false}
      SLACK_DEFAULT_CHANNEL: ${SLACK_DEFAULT_CHANNEL:-}
      SLACK_REPORTS_CHANNEL: ${SLACK_REPORTS_CHANNEL:-}
      SLACK_FILE_INGEST_MAX_BYTES: ${SLACK_FILE_INGEST_MAX_BYTES:-26214400}
      SLACK_APPROVALS_CHANNEL: ${SLACK_APPROVALS_CHANNEL:-}
      JARVIS_TELEGRAM_ENABLED: ${JARVIS_TELEGRAM_ENABLED:-false}
      OPENAI_API_KEY: ${OPENAI_API_KEY:-}
      JARVIS_TEXT_MODEL: ${JARVIS_TEXT_MODEL:-gpt-4o-mini}
      JARVIS_STT_MODEL: ${JARVIS_STT_MODEL:-gpt-4o-mini-transcribe}
      STT_BASE_URL: ${STT_BASE_URL:-}
      STT_MODEL: ${STT_MODEL:-}
      INTERNAL_BOOTSTRAP_SECRET: ${INTERNAL_BOOTSTRAP_SECRET:-}

      HERMES_DRIVER: ${HERMES_DRIVER:-native}

      AI_INSIGHTS_PROVIDER: ${AI_INSIGHTS_PROVIDER:-spark}
